task: Explain data drift to a product manager in at most 50 words, including one concrete example.
final_answer: Data drift means the real-world data a model sees slowly stops matching the data it learned from, so its predictions get worse. For example, a shopping recommender trained before the holidays may misjudge what people want in December. Teams watch for drift and retrain when it appears.

steps.name: draft
steps.input: Explain data drift to a product manager in at most 50 words, including one concrete example.
steps.output: Data drift happens when the data your model sees in production gradually stops looking like the data it was trained on. Because machine learning models learn statistical patterns from historical training data, any shift in input distributions, user behaviour, seasonality or upstream pipelines can silently reduce accuracy over time, which is why teams monitor feature distributions and retrain models regularly.
